keep: The idea is named up front: in parallel fuel decides a set's share of the kW and field its share of the kVAr ([^26]), both moved through the governor's and the AVR's set points ([^7]).

The cause of fuel moving kW is derived, not asserted: the rotor is locked in step, more fuel widens delta, and from lesson 3's drawing E sin delta = Xs x the in-step current, so power = E V sin delta / Xs. Checked on lesson 3's own case: 2.25 x sin 32.3 / 1.5 = 0.80 per unit = 504 kW.

One rule computes every kW readout: f = average setting - load / (2 x 210), each share 210 x (setting - f). Checked: 60.97 Hz and 300/300; +0.3 Hz gives 61.12 Hz, 331.5/268.5; +0.2 Hz gives 61.07 Hz, 321; 1% droop at 60.6 Hz with +0.3 gives 60.39 Hz, 426/174 (126 kW moved, four times 31.5); 62.8/62.4 gives 342/258 at 61.17 Hz; inset delta 18.5 and 20.5 degrees.

The kVAr view mirrors it with 30 kVAr a volt: 447.5 V settings give 440 V, 225/225; +2 V gives 441 V, 255/195, cross current 30 kVAr / (sqrt3 x 440) = 39.4 A; A's power factor 300 / 393.7 = 0.76, B's 0.84.

Every misconception in the brief has a DO screen with its own hints: fuel raises the frequency in parallel (5), mismatched settings (7, 14), two isochronous sets share (9), field raises the voltage in parallel (11).

Fourteen screens alternate SHOW 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 with DO 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, ending on two mixed typed puzzles (13 power factor, 14 the opposite nudge). Every figure answer is typed with slips; options only for what happens and which reading moves.

The battery-string analogy extends lesson 4's internal-resistance image to two strings (his Batteries course), reproduces the sharing and the small rise, and even the circulating current; its breaks are true.
